title: Business Intelligence Analysts
description: Produce financial and market intelligence by querying data repositories and generating periodic reports. Devise methods for identifying data patterns and trends in available information sources.

tasks.text: Identify and analyze industry or geographic trends with business strategy implications.
Collect business intelligence data from available industry reports, public information, field reports, or purchased sources.
Synthesize current business intelligence or trend data to support recommendations for action.
Analyze competitive market strategies through analysis of related product, market, or share trends.
Identify or monitor current and potential customers, using business intelligence tools.
Analyze technology trends to identify markets for future product development or to improve sales of existing products.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Manage timely flow of business intelligence information to users.
Document specifications for business intelligence or information technology reports, dashboards, or other outputs.
Maintain library of model documents, templates, or other reusable knowledge assets.
Generate standard or custom reports summarizing business, financial, or economic data for review by executives, managers, clients, and other stakeholders.
Create or review technical design documentation to ensure the accurate development of reporting solutions.
Maintain or update business intelligence tools, databases, dashboards, systems, or methods.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Provide technical support for existing reports, dashboards, or other tools.
Create business intelligence tools or systems, including design of related databases, spreadsheets, or outputs.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Disseminate information regarding tools, reports, or metadata enhancements.
Conduct or coordinate tests to ensure that intelligence is consistent with defined needs.
Communicate with customers, competitors, suppliers, professional organizations, or others to stay abreast of industry or business trends.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Airtable, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud EC2, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Web Services AWS software.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Advanced business application programming ABAP, Apache Groovy, C#, C++.

skills.name: Business intelligence and data analysis software
skills.def: Software to present, visualize, or analyze data to help businesses make informed decisions. Examples: Alteryx software, Apache Spark, Google Looker Analytics, IBM Cognos Impromptu.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Adobe ActionScript, Apache Ant, Apache Kafka, Business Objects Data Integrator.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Microsoft Dynamics, Microsoft Dynamics GP, NetSuite ERP, Oracle Fusion Applications.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: IBM SPSS Statistics, Minitab, Rogue Wave Software IMSL Numerical Libraries, SAS.
